A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same brain-graph autoencoder and latent-diffusion work, despite retitling and substantial expansion. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons, not document comparability.

before.justification: v1 reports original connectivity reconstruction, cognitive-state classification and graph-generation results in Section 3, plus seven-task classification and latent-distribution analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction, cognitive decoding, clinical classification, behavioral associations, generation and ablation results in Section 3, Tables 1–2 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The edge-conditioned encoder, attention pooling, memory decoder and latent DDPM remain. A bounded but substantive revision changes spatial reconstruction from both node features and connectivity, with weighted node/edge losses in v1 Equation 4 and Appendix A, to connectivity-only MSE in v2 Sections 2.1–2.3 and Appendix C. Neural-dynamics integration already produced results in v1; v2's detailed GRU specification does not establish that the extension itself is new.

E1.justification: v2 adds the BSNIP clinical cohort of 984 individuals, including healthy-control versus schizophrenia classification, and evaluates associations with task performance and composite cognition. HCP resting-state, working-memory and seven-task coverage are retained: the seven-task experiment already appeared in v1 Appendix B.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's GAE comparator, v2 Table 1 evaluates adapted Graphite, GRALE and GATE models, plus FC+UMAP and GraphMAE representation controls. These substantially broaden the actual reconstruction and latent-separability comparisons; Appendix D explains their adaptations.

E3.justification: The HCP split changes from 853/214 training/test subjects to 746/107/214 training/validation/test subjects, and working-memory decoding changes from SVM to logistic regression. v2 adds clinical cross-validation, multiple parcellation resolutions and controlled behavioral regressions. Latent-generation evaluation changes from training-distribution KS/covariance checks to held-out-test MMD and 1-NN comparisons, with additional matrix and spectral metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds removal tests for gradient alignment, edge conditioning and decoder memory across 64/100/150-node parcellations (Table 2). It also adds gradient-count sensitivity, range-versus-quantile stability checks, a reduced-rank analysis of metric covariation, and behavioral analyses of task reconfiguration. These substantially extend v1's feature comparisons and descriptive latent-space analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports KS p-values but does not specify repeated-run counts or reconstruction uncertainty. v2 newly reports four-seed means and standard deviations, variability across BSNIP folds, estimates across 50 generated subsamples, and FDR-adjusted behavioral tests. This establishes expanded statistical reporting, without establishing how many runs underlay v1.

E6.justification: Working-memory load accuracies change from 80%/86% without/with dynamics in v1 to 78.6%/89.7% in v2 under revised protocols, so these are not matched-setting gains. New results include BSNIP AUC 0.7370 ± 0.0483 (Table 1), a two-factor readout explaining R²=0.52, and extensive baseline, ablation, behavioral and generation results. Earlier radial-correlation and latent-covariance diagnostics are no longer reported.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.1 adds the mathematical qualification that Procrustes rotations prevent uniquely associating original diffusion eigenvalues with individual aligned gradient axes, motivating coordinate-range measurement. The underlying diffusion-map construction and attention/DDPM mathematics remain, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The compact-representation, cognitive-decoding and diffusion-generation claims remain. However, v2 explicitly adds task-induced reconfiguration and its global and directional relationships with cognitive performance as a main contribution in the Introduction and Conclusion. This extends v1's demonstrated state classification into behavioral significance that its Conclusion largely reserved for future work.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets spectral/topological covariation as preservation of information derived from the same FC matrix. It adds contrasting interpretations of diffuse task reconfiguration and gradient-directed variation in relation to cognition. Its limitations also newly address fixed node correspondence, dense-attention cost, preprocessing/template dependence and the need for broader external validation.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents parcellation construction, architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedules, checkpoint selection, GRU/DDPM configurations and baseline adaptations. It also specifies the gradient-only 20% edge threshold, reports computational costs, and supplies a code-repository pointer and data-access instructions. These substantially improve documentation beyond v1's brief appendix; newly disclosed settings do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around graph-level versus node-level autoencoding, oversmoothing, threshold sensitivity and alternative forms of geometry-guided learning. Added discussions and citations cover Graphite, GRALE, GraphMAE, neural dynamics and cognitive reconfiguration. v1's connectome-constrained simulation motivation and associated Lappalainen and Suarez citations are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with explicit contributions and much fuller methodological explanations. Spectral-method material moves from the appendix into the main Methods, experiments gain a dedicated protocol section and reorganized analyses, and the conclusion gains limitations. The appendices are reorganized into five focused sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 adds a framework schematic and two comparison tables, replaces reconstruction learning curves with uncertainty-bearing bar charts, and adds factor-loading, behavioral, alignment and stability displays. Generation figures are redesigned, while v1's seven-task confusion matrix and diffusion covariance/noising panels disappear.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited comparator coverage, missing repeated-run uncertainty and sparse implementation detail through broader baselines, component ablations, uncertainty reporting and detailed training documentation. Clinical and behavioral evidence, held-out latent-generation checks and explicit applicability limits strengthen the scientific case. Some earlier diagnostics are lost, and changed protocols prevent direct accuracy comparisons, but the gains in evidential support and reproducibility are substantial.
